entries.topic: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, "The Role of Decoherence in Quantum Mechanics"

claims.text: Decoherence is suppression of interference through entanglement with environment; environment interacts "in such a way that it could in principle be used as a measuring apparatus"; "decoherence as such does not provide a solution to the measurement problem"; no conscious observer required

sources.label: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, "The Role of Decoherence in Quantum Mechanics"

claims.text: von Neumann 1932; London and Bauer 1939; Wigner 1961/67; Wigner abandoned it late 1970s, called it "solipsism" (1982), crediting Zeh on decoherence; "largely discarded by modern physicists"; 2011 poll: 2 of 33 researchers
Wheeler proposed 1978; Jacques et al. 2007 realization; results reject naive realist wave-or-particle picture (Ma and Zeilinger); Wheeler did not accept retrocausal framing; Bohmian past unalterable
Aspect, Clauser, Zeilinger "for experiments with entangled photons, establishing the violation of Bell inequalities and pioneering quantum information science"

Penrose and Hameroff, 1990s; quantum processing in microtubules; Tegmark 2000 decoherence femtoseconds; 2022 Diósi–Penrose test found no radiation but Penrose original not ruled out; Churchland: "Pixie dust in the synapses..."
